video_title: HUGE  Expectations Returning To Rockets? + NBA Legends Explain Championship DNA

quotes.speaker: Rafael Stone
quotes.summary_phrase: Rafael Stone on managing team expectations with young players
quotes.excerpt: My job is to choose players, but it's not a simple as, I like this player, I like that player.
quotes.quote: It's the most important part of your job as a GM. My job is to choose players, but it's not a simple as, I like this player, I like that player. It's you've got an allocated amount of dollars and you've got a salary cap, you've got a luxury tax, now you've got a first apron and a second apron, and you have to allocate that. And those are the choices you make. And so, I don't know, so I just do my job is kind of how I think about it. I do think, I guess kind of the way that to tie this back to the Alperen Sengun trip, negotiating the deals, it's business and it's arms-length and I do it with their representatives. My relationship with the players is not business, and I think we've done a pretty good job of making sure that our players understand where I'm coming from so that, look, everybody wants to be richer, and I don't begrudge anyone that, and I never begrudge someone saying no. But it's also important to me that we be realistic.

quotes.speaker: Rafael Stone
quotes.summary_phrase: Rafael Stone on the expectations for Kevin Durant in Houston
quotes.excerpt: He understood coming in that this wasn't going to be a situation where we're trading for him.
quotes.quote: Obviously when you trade for somebody of Kevin Durant's stature, it's very important that you have good conversations coming in about expectations. And he understood coming in that this wasn't going to be a situation where we're trading for him and now we're going to go get 75 veteran players to play with him, which sometimes happens, but it's not like that has a great track record of success. And so, he understood that he was coming in to play with a bunch of younger guys and that the team was probably going to look the way it looks now. And it has. And is best I can tell, you guys can ask him, but he really enjoys them.

quotes.speaker: Rafael Stone
quotes.summary_phrase: Rafael Stone on Amen Thompson's development and impact
quotes.excerpt: Since about halfway through his rookie year, we've been a materially better team when he's on the court.
quotes.quote: I think he's a very, very good basketball player. Since about halfway through his rookie year, we've been a materially better team when he's on the court. And he keeps getting better. I thought he had a really good year last year. He just got better and better and better and better. And he helps our team on the court in literally every way you can. We turn the ball over less, we turn the other team over more, we rebound better, we shoot a higher percentage, we shoot free throws better. Everything's better with Amen Thompson. So yeah, we're very, very high on him.

quotes.speaker: Jabari Smith Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Jabari Smith Jr. on NBA parity and team health
quotes.excerpt: I think it just a testament to how good the NBA is honestly.
quotes.quote: I think it just a testament to how good the NBA is honestly. You can't really predict what's going to happen. You just can't really look at it. You got to keep your head down and work. We know we have the talent, we know we have the pieces to get it done. You know, it's just on us to be selfless, put all our egos aside and just put it together and make it work. You know, we have the roster. You can look at it on paper, it looks good, but it's just on us to put it together honestly.

quotes.speaker: Jabari Smith Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Jabari Smith Jr. on team chemistry and communication
quotes.excerpt: It's just a brotherhood thing you got to build and when you have that brotherhood you can talk.
quotes.quote: I think it's how you talk to your teammates and how you receive messages. Sometimes you can feel attacked when a teammate gets on you or when you know, when your teammate expects different things from you. But I think it's just how you receive the message and I think that comes with how close you are to somebody. If you may talk to your best friend differently than you talk to, you know, me. You know what I'm saying? So it's just a brotherhood thing you got to build and when you have that brotherhood you can talk to your teammates differently and receive it differently. And you hold them to a different pedestal and then you just you want to show it for them more when you're connected like that.

quotes.speaker: Naji Marshall
quotes.summary_phrase: Naji Marshall on developing his floater and finishing
quotes.excerpt: The floater is a thing that's been working for me for a long time.
quotes.quote: I would say opportunity. Playing with the Pelicans, I was playing behind a couple of guys so I didn't really get that many shots. Just opportunity just to be out there and if I was out there, you know, it was just to get those guys a break, which I respect and I appreciate. But I think just the more opportunity came, the more I was just to spread light on my game as a whole. And the floater is a thing that's been working for me for a long time and so just being able to get to it at the highest level, you know, you got to keep it simple. Find things that work for you and repeat it over and over. And Kyrie Irving, he's got an elite 5-to-9 foot game. He's taught me a lot, especially with finishing. Since I've gotten here, my finish has been at the rim in that 5-to-9 feet and that's definitely credited to Kyrie.

quotes.speaker: Shawn Marion
quotes.summary_phrase: Shawn Marion on the shift to positionless basketball
quotes.excerpt: The game is definitely shifted to where it's completely positionless basketball.
quotes.quote: As y'all seen the game shift drastically since then to now, what is the pros and cons to what y'all seeing now? Because the game is definitely shifted to where it's completely positionless basketball. And it's wild, you know, the pace and space. We talked about the seven seconds or less Suns, really kind of being on the forefront of that. Honestly, Don Nelson also, RIP, he was he was at the forefront of this positionless thing. But when you guys came in Phoenix and were just launching threes, we felt like, oh my god, can you the threes you took per game would rank dead last in the league by a wide margin now.

quotes.speaker: Shawn Marion
quotes.summary_phrase: Shawn Marion on the business side of NBA contracts
quotes.excerpt: I know I'm on the owner's side now too though. So you don't make money until you sell the team.
quotes.quote: I know I'm on the owner's side now too though. So you don't make money until you sell the team. Most of the money that's recycled every season is goes back to run the team. And that's what I say. If you can afford to fund a contender and you've got that kind of team, sell. Your agent was the late great Dan Fagan. Yes he was. Now, the Dan Fagan I've talked about on this podcast, fascinating guy, tragically died in a car accident. What do you imagine if when you were in your prime, and you were on a max contract? Yeah, all it takes is one team. So they weren't up for when I was up though. I get what you're saying, but I understand. So I I didn't realize I thought it was just two years left on his deal. I know he's a free agent. Yeah, so okay. It's just a year plus a player option.

quotes.speaker: Carlos Boozer
quotes.summary_phrase: Carlos Boozer on advice for his son Cameron Boozer
quotes.excerpt: I just hope him to to take in these moments like be where your feet are.
quotes.quote: I'm proud of him. First off, first off, I know this has been his dream to be in this position, to be in the NBA and have a chance to play for a team that loves him. And so, I just hope him to to take in these moments like be where your feet are. Be present, enjoy these moments because they go by so fast. I still remember my first game against Sacramento back in 2002 when they had Chris Webber. And I was, you know, 20 something years ago. So I just hope him to be where your feet are, be as present as you can be, enjoy every moment, because they go by so fast.

quotes.speaker: Carlos Boozer
quotes.summary_phrase: Carlos Boozer on Cameron Boozer's drive to win
quotes.excerpt: If you ask them what you want to be known for, he's going to say that exactly.
quotes.quote: B, when you talk to him and you guys are probably interviewing him a lot, if you ask them what you want to be known for, like what your legacy you want to be, you know, 10, 20 years down the road, he's going to say that exactly. I want to be known as a winner. That's all he cares about. He doesn't care about the statistics, he doesn't care about whose name is in the paper, he wants to win. And he's always been cut like that from the very first day.
